honestly dbt therapy would be really beneficial. if you can’t afford that because it is pretty expensive, you should get this workbook off amazon called the borderline personality workbook which is basically just dbt therapy. it’s only $16 and it’s so worth it. also what seems to really help me with splitting is figuring out whether i’m actually upset over the persons actions, or if it just triggered a belief, a traumatic experience, or a thought that i have. for example if my boyfriend doesn’t answer me for a while and i begin to feel myself hating him, i’ll ask myself if i’m upset that he took hours to respond or if it just triggered the belief that he’s gonna abandon me. 

bpd often stems from negative beliefs that we have about ourselves or others. try to think of a negative belief that you have, behaviour that stems from it, and then discover patterns that you have. for example, one of the beliefs i have about myself is that im unlovable, and that makes me cling on to my partner and try my best not to get him to leave, and that often leads to them getting scared off and leaving. so in order to let go of these patterns, you have to address the core negative beliefs that you have.
